nodes.name: Hydrothermal NiCo-(MoO4)2- LDH synthesis
nodes.procedure: Ni(NO3)2·6H2O (0.05 mmol), Co(NO3)2·6H2O (0.1 mmol), Na2MoO4·2H2O (0.1 mmol) and urea (145 mg) were dispersed into 35 mL deionized water, and the mixed solution was stirred to form homogeneous solution, and then it was transferred into 50 mL Teflon container with washed CFC. Teflon reactor containing carbon cloths and solution was heated up to 110°C for 6 h in oven. After hydrothermal reaction, the CFC with production was washed by deionized water for several times and dried in vacuum oven at 60°C for 12 h.

nodes.name: Sulfuration of LDH to NiCoMoS4
nodes.procedure: The obtained NiCo - (MoO4)^2 - LDH/CFC was mixed with 100 mg of sulfur powder in ceramic boat, and then annealed at 350°C with heating rate of 5°C min-1 under N2 for 1 h to form Ni0.33Co0.67MoS4 / CFC.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns show NiCo-(MoO₄)²⁻ LDH/CFC with peaks at 34.01° and 59.79° matching NiCo LDH (JCPDS: 14-0191) with slight lattice shifts from interlayer MoO₄²⁻. Ni₀.₃₃Co₀.₆₇MoS₄/CFC shows peaks at 13.4°, 20.4°, 22.3°, 26.9°, 29.4°, 30.9°, 32.9°, 35.9° assigned to CoMoO₄ planes (JCPDS: 15-0439) with slight shifts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From XRD patterns (Fig. 2a), CFC and NSs on CFC all possessed a broad peak at region of 20∼30°... The XRD pattern of NSs in first step showed two diffraction peaks locating at 34.01° and 59.79°, which can be matched with NiCo LDH... After vulcanization of NiCo-(MoO₄)² LDH/CFC, diffraction peaks of samples at 20 of 13.4°, 20.4°, 22.3°, 26.9°, 29.4°, 30.9°, 32.9° and 35.9°, which were assigned to planes of CoMoO₄ (JCPDS: 15-0439)

nodes.characterization_summary: FE-SEM shows NiCo-(MoO₄)²⁻ LDH forms uniform nanosheets on CFC carbon fibers (10 μm diameter). After vulcanization, Ni₀.₃₃Co₀.₆₇MoS₄ maintains nanosheet morphology.
nodes.evidence_snippet: low-magnification and high magnification SEM images (inset of Fig. 1c) indicated that NSs grew uniformly on CFC (Fig. 1c), and NiCo-(MoO₄)²⁻ LDH ones on CFC were prepared. After vulcanization of products, their morphology still remained NSs, which was composed of Ni₀.₃₃Co₀.₆₇MoS₄ (Fig. 1d).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM of NiCo-(MoO₄)²⁻ LDH shows poor crystallization. Ni₀.₃₃Co₀.₆₇MoS₄/CFC TEM reveals nanosheets composed of small nanoparticles; HRTEM shows lattice spacings of 0.28 nm (022), 0.29 nm (310), 0.33 nm (002) confirming polycrystalline structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM and selected-area electron diffraction (SAED) images of LDH indicated the sample was poor crystallization (Fig. S1), resulting in weak diffraction peaks. ... The high resolution TEM (HRTEM) images of Ni₀.₃₃Co₀.₆₇MoS₄/CFC revealed the lattice planes showed polycrystalline features of samples.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiCo-(MoO₄)²⁻ LDH/CFC: Co 2p₃/₂ 781.4 eV (Co³⁺), 2p₁/₂ 796.8 eV (Co³⁺), auger 773.7 eV; Ni 2p₃/₂ 856.1 eV, 2p₁/₂ 873.9 eV (Ni³⁺/Ni²⁺); Mo 3d₅/₂ 232.5 eV, 3d₃/₂ 235.6 eV (Mo⁶⁺), Ni/Co/Mo = 0.33:0.67:1. Ni₀.₃₃Co₀.₆₇MoS₄/CFC: Co 2p Co³⁺ (779.5, 794.5 eV), Co²⁺ (781.3, 796.6 eV); Ni 2p Ni³⁺/Ni²⁺; Mo 3d₅/₂ 229.4 eV, 3d₃/₂ 232.8 eV (Mo⁶⁺); S 2p₁/₂ 163.5 eV, 2p₃/₂ 162.1 eV (M-S).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Co 2p spectrum was split to Co 2p₃/₂, Co 2p₁/₂ and auger peak at 781.4, 796.8 and 773.7 eV... In Ni 2p XPS spectrum, two signals appear at Ni 2p₃/₂ (856.1 eV) and Ni 2p₁/₂ (873.9 eV)... XPS spectrum of NiCo-(MoO₄)²⁻ LDH/CFC showed that presents two peaks appearing at 235.6 eV and 232.5 eV... Two peaks located at 779.5 and 794.5 eV, which were ascribed to Co³⁺... from Mo 3d spectrum of sample (Fig. 3c), two strong peaks at 229.4 eV and 232.8 eV... Spectrum of S 2P (Fig. 3d) showed the binding energies at 163.5 and 162.1 eV

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS of NiCo-(MoO₄)²⁻ LDH/CFC shows C, Co, Ni, Mo, O elements. Ni₀.₃₃Co₀.₆₇MoS₄/CFC EDS confirms Ni/Co/Mo/S ratio 0.33:0.67:1:4 with uniform elemental mapping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: energy dispersive spectrum (EDS) of NiCo-(MoO₄)²⁻ LDH/CFC showed five elements of C, Co, Ni, Mo and O... EDS spectrum of sample contained four elements of Co, Ni, Mo and S with Ni/Co/Mo/S atomic ratio of 0.33:0.67:1:4 (Fig. S6).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS confirms Ni/Co/Mo atomic ratio of 0.33:0.67:1 consistent with XPS and EDS for both NiCo-(MoO₄)²⁻ LDH/CFC and Ni₀.₃₃Co₀.₆₇MoS₄/CFC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the atomic ratio of Ni/Co/Mo was consistent with the result of ICP-MS (0.33:0.67:1) (Table. S2).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni₀.₃₃Co₀.₆₇MoS₄/CFC specific surface area is 140.6 m²/g, larger than NiCo₂S₄/CFC at 48.2 m²/g.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ni₀.₃₃Co₀.₆₇MoS₄ NSs (SSA: 140.6 m²g⁻¹) possessed larger specific surface area than NiCo₂S₄ NWs (SSA: 48.2 m²g⁻¹), which exposed more active sites (Fig. S14).

nodes.characterization_summary: FTIR of NiCo-(MoO₄)²⁻ LDH shows O-H stretching at 3450 cm⁻¹ and broad absorption below 1000 cm⁻¹ for Mo-O, Co-O, Ni-O asymmetric stretching.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From Fourier transform infrared spectrum (FTIR) (Fig. S2), the large band centered at 3450 cm⁻¹ was assigned to the O-H stretching modes, while the broad absorption below 1000 cm⁻¹ for asymmetric stretching (Mo-O, Co-O and Ni-O).

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman of NiCo-(MoO₄)²⁻ LDH shows peaks at 876, 907 cm⁻¹ for molybdate hydrogen bonded and chemically bonded to interlayer water and LDH surface, and 854 cm⁻¹ for molybdate anti-symmetric stretching.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman spectrum (Fig. S3) of LDH indicated that 876 and 907 cm⁻¹ were assigned to molybdate hydrogen bonded and chemically bonded to interlayer water molecules and the NiCo LDH surface, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni₀.₃₃Co₀.₆₇MoS₄/CFC shows lowest charge transfer resistance R_ct = 3.86 Ω at -0.6 V vs Ag/AgCl for HER and lowest R_ct at 0.5 V for OER among tested catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ni₀.₃₃Co₀.₆₇MoS₄/CFC revealed lowest charge transfer resistance of 3.86 Ω. Compared with other catalysts, the charge transfer resistance of NiCo₂S₄/CFC (21.01 Ω) was more than three times larger... From the result of EIS, catalyst of Ni₀.₃₃Co₀.₆₇MoS₄/CFC possessed lowest charge transfer resistance among all catalysts (Fig. S13).
